summary: The Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act (TAS Act) aims to improve taxpayer services provided by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). The bill establishes new technological tools for taxpayers and tax professionals, updates IRS procedures regarding collections, appeals, and penalties, modifies rules for tax return preparers and whistleblowers, expands the authority and jurisdiction of the U.S. Tax Court, and provides specific relief for Americans abroad, hostages, and small businesses.

affected_groups.effect: Receive better online access to account information, real-time wait-time dashboards, waived installment agreement fees for low-income individuals, streamlined collection alternative notices, and enhanced dispute resolution options.
Subject to new PTIN and EFIN validation rules, increased penalties for improper alterations, misappropriation of refunds, or invalid identifying numbers, and new background and education standards.
Benefit from required studies on simplifying foreign account reporting, extended periods to request math error abatements, and pre-assessment appeal rights for foreign information return penalties.
Have tax deadlines, interest, and penalties postponed or abated, alongside an established program to refund previously paid penalties.
Receive de novo Tax Court review standards for award determinations, mandatory whistleblower anonymity before the Tax Court, exemption from budget sequestration, and interest on delayed awards.

key_provisions: Requires the IRS to digitize paper tax returns and correspondence using optical character recognition, and create a public real-time dashboard tracking call wait times and backlogs.
Expands online account access and mobile applications for taxpayers and authorized representatives to view six years of tax documents, notices, and returns, and to upload responses.
Eliminates installment agreement fees for individuals with adjusted gross incomes at or below 250 percent of the applicable poverty level.
Increases the U.S. Tax Court small dispute threshold from $50,000 to $100,000 with annual inflation adjustments, and authorizes the Tax Court to hear certain refund suits up to $2,000,000.
Grants the National Taxpayer Advocate direct-hire authority for attorneys and personnel decisions, and guarantees TAS access to requested IRS information, meetings, and legal advice.
Enforces stricter rules and penalties for tax return preparers, including background checks, continuing education requirements, and validating Electronic Filing Identification Numbers (EFINs).
Postpones tax deadlines, waives interest and penalties, and provides a refund program for U.S. nationals who were held hostage or wrongfully detained abroad.
missing_information: Exact numerical estimates of the total cost or budgetary impact of implementing the digital platforms, dashboards, and staffing expansions.
Specific poverty level dollar thresholds that the Secretary of the Treasury will establish for waiving installment agreement fees.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act (TAS Act) aims to improve taxpayer services provided by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). The bill establishes new technological tools for taxpayers and tax professionals, updates IRS procedures regarding collections, appeals, and penalties, modifies rules for tax return preparers and whistleblowers, expands the authority and jurisdiction of the U.S. Tax Court, and provides specific relief for Americans abroad, hostages, and small businesses.
summary_detail.significance: The TAS Act implements sweeping operational changes to the IRS, taxpayer advocacy offices, and the federal judicial review process for tax disputes. By expanding digital services, altering penalty and collection protocols, and granting broader powers to the Taxpayer Advocate and the Tax Court, the legislation significantly reshapes the administrative and legal landscape of federal tax administration.
